items.title: A global guide to birthdays that nearly need a ministry of their own
items.summary: For most 76-year-olds, a birthday means cake, a call from the grandchildren and perhaps a gentle argument about sugar. For Prime Minister Narendra Modi, it now means a month-long national exercise in seva . The BJP’s Seva Sankalp Abhiyan marks 25 years since Modi first took public office as Gujarat chief minister. Ministries and state governments have been roped in, more than 500 locations are expected to participate, and the programme comes with 14 separate “modules” covering everything from health camps and cleanliness drives to overseas mahayagyas . Delhi has tied the celebrations to development projects worth around Rs 13,820 crore; Haryana has handed each deputy commissioner Rs 10 lakh for the campaign. There are diyas by the lakh, including a 5,000-diya portrait of Modi in Assam and 76,000 lamps at a midnight Ahmedabad event. This is not particularly new. Heads of states have been finding creative ways to turn their birthdays into public spectacle across history. Ancient kings commissioned monuments and rituals. Medieval courts turned royal anniversaries into displays of wealth and divine favour. Modern dictators perfected the genre, with choreographed parades and compulsory adulation. Democracies have had their gentler versions too: public service campaigns and the occasional flattering newspaper supplement. The difference, of course, is who is paying and what exactly is being celebrated. Modi’s own birthday machinery has steadily expanded. As Gujarat chief minister, he generally kept the occasion low-key . After the BJP named him its prime ministerial candidate in 2013, the celebrations grew into week-long service drives; later came 21-day Seva aur Samarpan campaigns and fortnight-long Seva Pakhwadas . Now we have a month. At this rate, the 80th birthday may require a fiscal year. So, before the candles become a national infrastructure project, let’s take a brief tour through history to see how rulers and political leaders have handled the awkward business of getting older in public. items.title: ‘प्राइमटाइम पर मुझे एंटी-नेशनल बताया गया': सुधीर चौधरी पर 5 करोड़ रुपये का मुकदमा करने वाले शेरावत
items.summary: 27 जुलाई को सुधीर चौधरी के प्राइमटाइम शो ‘डिकोड’ में यूपीएससी अभ्यर्थी और छात्र कार्यकर्ता विजय शेरावत को उस शख्स के तौर पर दिखाया गया, जिसने कथित तौर पर संसद को “उखाड़ फेंकने” और भारत को नेपाल बनाने की बात कही थी. लेकिन शेरावत के मुताबिक, इसमें एक बड़ी समस्या थी कि वीडियो में मौजूद व्यक्ति शेरावत नहीं था. दिल्ली हाईकोर्ट में दायर अपने मामले में शेरावत ने कहा है कि ये टिप्पणियां किसी और व्यक्ति ने की थीं. उनका आरोप है कि इसके बावजूद ‘डिकोड’ के प्रसारण में इन टिप्पणियों को उनके नाम से जोड़ते हुए उनकी तस्वीर का इस्तेमाल किया गया. शेरावत का कहना है कि प्रसारण से पहले फुटेज का सत्यापन नहीं किया गया और न ही उनका पक्ष जानने की कोशिश की गई. उन्होंने सुधीर चौधरी और डीडी न्यूज़ समेत अन्य प्रतिवादियों से 5 करोड़ रुपये के हर्जाने की मांग की है. साथ ही, प्रसारण को आगे प्रकाशित और प्रसारित करने पर रोक लगाने की मांग भी की है. अदालत ने चौधरी, डीडी न्यूज़ और अन्य प्रतिवादियों को नोटिस जारी किया है. मामले की अगली सुनवाई 22 सितंबर को सूचीबद्ध है. हालांकि, शेरावत के लिए ‘डिकोड’ का वह एक एपिसोड यहीं खत्म नहीं हुआ. शेरावत ने न्यूज़लॉन्ड्री से बातचीत में कहा, “मैं पूरी तरह बर्बाद हो गया हूं. प्रसारण के बाद क्लिप सोशल मीडिया पर तेजी से फैली और इसके तुरंत बाद मुझे धमकियां मिलने लगीं." वह आगे कहते हैं, “एक एंकर के एक बयान ने पूरी दुनिया के सामने मुझे एंटी-नेशनल घोषित कर दिया.” शेरावत के मुताबिक, इस मामले ने उनका वह समय भी छीन लिया, जिसे वह यूपीएससी सिविल सेवा परीक्षा की तैयारी में लगाना चाहते थे. उनका कहना है कि पिछले कुछ महीनों में परीक्षा की तैयारी के बजाय उन्हें वकीलों से मिलने और अदालत की सुनवाइयों के लिए जाना पड़ा. शेरावत के लिए यह मामला सिर्फ अपना नाम साफ कराने तक सीमित नहीं है. उनका कहना है कि वह इस मामले के जरिए पत्रकारिता में जवाबदेही तय करने के लिए एक मिसाल कायम करना चाहते हैं. विजय शेरावत के साथ पूरा इंटरव्यू देखें. एनएल इंटरव्यू: बिहार एसआईआर, उपराष्ट्रपति के इस्तीफे और ‘एंटी नेशनल पत्रकारों’ पर भाजपा सांसद रामचंद्र जांगड़ा प्रोफेसर लक्ष्मण यादव: 14 साल पढ़ाया, 14 मिनट के एक इंटरव्यू में बाहर कर दिया

items.title: Lack of charging points deterring people from buying electric cars: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday observed that the lack of charging facilities was discouraging people from buying electric vehicles (EVs), as it underlined the need to provide the necessary infrastructure for a shift away from fossil-fuel vehicles. A Bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe made the remarks while hearing a petition concerning the allotment of land by the Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation (MIDC), where the allotment of space for an EV charging facility came up for discussion. Justice PS Narasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe During the hearing, Justice Narasimha recounted a conversation with a person whom he had advised to consider buying an electric car. "I was suggesting to somebody who was wanting to buy a car. I said, now it's better that you go for EV car. He said, it's very good and super for you to say, but in my place or wherever I go, where is the charging point? There are no charging points," Justice Narasimha said. The judge then remarked that the absence of charging facilities was holding people back from buying electric cars. "Because there are no charging points, people are not buying electric cars. "But then it doesn't really happen if you don't provide the facilities," he observed. The judge then referred to the possibility of providing EV charging facilities at the Supreme Court itself. "If you park your car in the Supreme Court here, by the time you discuss the matter, you have to get your car charged. That will be advantageous. items.title: Delhi court grants bail to US national Matthew Aaron VanDyke in Myanmar terror training case
items.summary: A Delhi court on Friday granted default bail to Matthew Aaron Van Dyke, a US national who was arrested by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) in March this year. Special NIA Judge Prashant Sharma of the Rouse Avenue Court granted bail to Van Dyke on a personal bond of ₹1 lakh and a surety of the same amount. In its order, the Court noted that the chargesheet filed by the NIA was "piecemeal" as it pertained to Section 21 and 23 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025 only. It said that as the NIA is still investigating the offences under Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), it cannot be concluded that Van Dyke is not entitled to default bail. "As such, investigating agency cannot circumvent sec. 187(3) BNSS (erstwhile sec. 167(2) CrPC) by filing incomplete charge-sheet, for the purpose of denying default bail to applicant/ accused Matthew Aaron Van Dyke," the Court said. The Court said that while on bail, Van Dyke must stay in Delhi and appear before the NIA whenever required. Further, the Court added that all the other co-accused persons in the case are also entitled to default bail. Van Dyke was arrested by the NIA at Kolkata airport on March 13, 2026, alongside six Ukrainian nationals arrested at Lucknow and Delhi airports the same day. As per his own website, he had served in the Iraq War and Libya's civil war, and he founded a Washington, DC-based security consulting firm called Sons of Liberty International, which says it trains vulnerable populations to defend against terrorist and insurgent groups. It has been reported that the firm also advised Ukraine's military on non-lethal equipment between 2022 and 2023. The group was accused of entering India's Mizoram state without valid permits and then illegally crossing into Myanmar, where they allegedly provided drone-warfare training to ethnic armed groups fighting Myanmar's military government. The case was initially registered under Section 18 of the UAPA, but in the first chargesheet filed in the case, the anti-terror agency only referred to violation of the provisions of the Immigration and Foreigners Act. It later clarified that terror charges have not been dropped against the accused. Advocates Rohit Dandriyal and Rohit Gour represented Van Dyke. NIA was represented by Special Public Prosecutor (SPP) Rahul Tyagi, as well as advocates Ankit Gautam and Jatin.

items.title: Can POSH Act cover women lawyers? What Supreme Court suggested
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday observed that the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 (POSH Act) cannot be applied in a straitjacket manner to women advocates [ Seema Joshi v. Bar Council of India ]. A Bench of Justices BV Nagarathna and AG Masih suggested a separate regulatory framework to protect female lawyers practicing in courts and tribunals across the country. The Court called for a joint consultation among various stakeholders to draft a comprehensive set of regulations for women in the legal profession, while examining the existing gender sensitisation rules. Justice bv nagarathna and Justice augustine george masih The Court made the observations while hearing a plea seeking statutory protections for women advocates. Examining the Gender Sensitisation and Sexual Harassment of Women at the Supreme Court of India (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Regulations, 2013, the Bench pointed out that the current framework is strictly limited to the top court's precincts. "In order to have a wider coverage of these regulations in so far as the High Courts and all courts under district judiciary as well as tribunals under Centre and State governments, other quasi-judicial authorities etc., it is necessary that a separate set of regulations are made as we find that POSH provisions cannot be applied in a straitjacket manner for the aggrieved women who belong to the legal profession, " the Court said. To address this gap, the apex court requested counsel to hold a joint consultation and draft a uniform set of regulations applicable across judicial, quasi-judicial and tribunal forums. Advocate Radhika Gautam, appearing for the Bar Council of India (BCI), submitted that she would seek instructions and endeavour to bring about a common regulation for women advocates. "We also request BCI counsel to ascertain from State Bar Councils as to whether any extant regulations are being implemented in this regard," the Court ordered.

items.title: NCLT sends Bira, creditors to mediation in insolvency case
items.summary: The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) at New Delhi has sent Bira and its creditors to mediation to explore a settlement of insolvency proceedings pending against the company. " It is made clear that if no settlement is arrived between the parties in the meeting directed to be scheduled, no further indulgence would be shown in the matter ," the Tribunal said. Counsel appearing for the company submitted that settlement discussions were being held with the creditors. However, several creditors expressed reservations about the proposal. Unity Small Finance Bank placed before the Tribunal a September 10 letter to show that an offer of ₹3 crore had been made against dues of over ₹19.04 crore. It argued that the proposal could not be regarded as a serious or plausible settlement offer. Axis Bank, on the other hand, informed the Tribunal that it had received a settlement offer and was considering it. Counsel for some of the other creditors alleged that the settlement attempts were only intended to buy time. They raised apprehensions that the company's assets could be pilfered. items.title: Supreme Court stays P&H High Court verdict striking down Section 147A of Income Tax Act
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday stayed a Punjab and Haryana High Court judgment that had struck down Section 147A of the Income Tax Act, 1961 as unconstitutional [Union of India and Others v. Bharat Industrial Enterprises Private Limited] A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran passed the order on a challenge filed by the Central government against the High Court ruling. “ The impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court shall remain stayed, subject to the condition that the assessment and reassessment proceedings shall not proceed further until the final disposal of the main matter, ” the apex court ordered. Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice Vinod Chandran The dispute arose from the issue of whether notices for reopening income-tax assessments can be issued by a taxpayer’s local Jurisdictional Assessing Officer (JAO) or must be issued through the Faceless Assessing Officer or National Faceless Assessment Centre (NFAC). The issue arose from Section 151A of the Income Tax Act and the e-Assessment of Income Escaping Assessment Scheme notified under it on March 29, 2022. Under the scheme, notices under Section 148 for reopening assessments must be issued through automated allocation and in a faceless manner. Taxpayers then challenged reassessment notices issued directly by their jurisdictional assessing officers. However, the parliament introduced Section 147A through the Finance Act, 2026, with retrospective effect from April 1, 2021. The provision contained a non-obstante clause and clarified that, notwithstanding any court judgment, Section 151A or any scheme framed under it, the assessing officer for such proceedings would mean an officer other than the NFAC or its assessment units. On September 10, the Punjab and Haryana High Court struck down Section 147A as unconstitutional. It held that parliament could not override judicial decisions without removing the legal basis on which they were delivered. The High Court found that Section 151A and the 2022 scheme continued to require reassessment notices to be issued through randomised automated allocation and in a faceless manner. It held that merely introducing Section 147A with a non-obstante clause did not cure the underlying defect or resolve the conflict. The Union government challenged this ruling before the Supreme Court which stayed the verdict. The Court has listed the plea for final hearing on December 3. items.title: J&K High Court establishes Delhi office for coordination with Supreme Court, Central government
items.summary: The High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh on Friday sanctioned a resident office at New Delhi for better coordination and communication with the Supreme Court and the Union government at the national level. The office will function under the supervision and control of an officer designated as Registrar (Headquarters), New Delhi and report to the Chief Justice through the Registrar General. In an order issued on Friday, Chairman of the J&K Sales Tax Appellate Tribunal Amit Kumar Gupta was asked to function as Registrar (Headquarters), New Delhi till further orders. As per the High Court, the resident office has been established for following purposes: 1. Establish and maintain a secure channel for transmission and handling of confidential communications and sensitive matters requiring direct interaction between the High Court and the Supreme Court; 2. Maintain regular liaison with the Supreme Court Registry; the Department of Justice, constitutional authorities, judicial institutions, ministries, departments and other agencies in New Delhi; 3. Facilitate handling of administrative and institutional matters requiring coordination at the national level; 4. Coordinate with standing counsel and other counsel engaged on behalf of the High Court before the Supreme Court; 5. Monitor the progress of cases involving the High Court and ensure timely transmission of records, instructions, comments and responses; 6. items.title: Physical presence not necessary for witness examination if VC can facilitate cross-examination: Madras HC
items.summary: The Madras High Court recently observed that a witness need not be physically present before a trial court for cross-examination if it can be effectively conducted through video conferencing [ Narayanasamy Vs Balasundaram ]. Justice N Anand Venkatesh added that even complex cases involving several documents cannot be kept out of video-conference hearings merely because cross-examination of witnesses may be difficult. "A stage has come where any proceedings can be conducted through the VC mode. Several complex arbitration cases involving large turnover and several volumes of documents are being conducted conveniently through the online/VC mode. This is the reason as to why the Madras High Court Video Conferencing Rules, 2026 were notified and the same provide for the procedure to be followed to record the evidence through the VC mode. Hence, the Court below can never dispense with or refuse to conduct examination of witnesses through the VC mode just because the case involves several documents or complex issues," the September 9 ruling said. It dismissed a petition made by the doctor's legal opponents (petitioners), who opposed his cross-examination through video conference and insisted that he should return to India for the trial proceedings. The Court found that the doctor had been in India on several hearing dates, but that the petitioners had not used these opportunities to physically cross-examine him. “ It is quite surprising that the petitioners are insisting for the physical presence of the first respondent/plaintiff whereas the petitioners missed the bus when the first respondent/plaintiff was, in fact, present physically in India at least for three hearings," the Court said. items.title: Not in favour of setting deadlines for High Courts to decide cases: Supreme Court
items.summary: Appellate courts must respect the heavy docket pressures faced by courts below them and should avoid imposing strict timelines for disposing off cases, the Supreme Court said on Friday. A Bench of Justices BV Nagarathna and AG Masih said that the Supreme Court is averse to imposing deadlines for High Courts or district courts to decide cases. The Court made the observation while hearing a plea by a man involved in a matrimonial dispute, seeking the return of his passport and the expeditious hearing of his quashing petition pending before the High Court. When counsel for the petitioner requested the apex court to direct the High Court to dispose of the matter within a strict four-week timeline, Justice Nagarathna declined to issue such a mandate. "We don’t even like to indicate to district judges about dates for disposal. We will not do it for the High Court also. Every judge has their own docket to be complied with every day. You can request the High Court," she remarked. Recalling her own tenure as a judge in the High Court, Justice Nagarathna highlighted how fixed-timeline orders from higher courts are perceived by trial and High Court benches. "When we were there in the High Court, we remember how we would treat such orders where the Supreme Court used to direct. Let us be frank. Our feeling then we do not want to replicate in a different way just because we are sitting here," she said. Justice bv nagarathna and Justice augustine george masih The petitioner approached the top court contending that multiple legal proceedings were underway arising out of matrimonial discord, including a look out circular (LOC). The counsel argued that despite an explicit order of protection granted by the High Court, the petitioner was arrested following his father's demise and his passport was impounded, severely impacting his livelihood. It was further submitted that the High Court had repeatedly adjourned the quashing petition along with the application seeking the return of the passport, eventually deferring the matter to February 2027. The Supreme Court, while refusing to set a fixed date, granted liberty to the petitioner to move the High Court for an earlier hearing date. items.title: Kerala High Court refuses interim bail to Reporter TV MD Anto Augustine

[Anto Augustine v State of Kerala] Justice Kauser Edappagath declined urgent relief after the prosecution informed the court that it has moved an application seeking police custody of Augustine and that he is scheduled to be produced before the magistrate court on Saturday. In view of the custody application, the Court declined to grant interim bail at this stage. However, the Court enquired whether Augustine could be connected to the property from which the alleged liquor was recovered, particularly in view of claim that the property had been sold in SARFESI proceedings in 2022. The judge then asked the prosecution to produce material if available to establish that Augustine was actually in position of the property. The matter will be heard next on September 22. He later moved a bail before a trial court, which rejected the application earlier today. This prompted him to approach the High Court. Augustine was arrested a day after a Special Investigation Team (SIT) of Kerala Police searched his offices and residences. The search was conducted as part of a probe into alleged financial fraud in connection with a failed football event with the Argentinian national team and footballer Lionel Messi. Augustine's Reporter Broadcasting Company was the main commercial sponsor of the event. During a raid reportedly conducted at Augustine's family home in Wayanad, police uncovered roughly 67 litres of foreign liquor and wine, which exceeds the legally permissible limit for personal possession. The Excise Department arrested Augustine in the early hours of Thursday. items.title: Ex-DGP Tomin Thachankary moves Kerala High Court challenging conviction in disproportionate assets case
items.summary: Former Kerala Director General of Police (DGP) Tomin J Thachankary has moved the Kerala High Court challenging a Vigilance Court ruling that convicted him in a disproportionate assets case. Kottayam Enquiry Commissioner and Special Judge (Vigilance) KV Rajaneesh had on Thursday passed the verdict after finding that there was a disproportionate income of over ₹30 lakh, which comes up to over 50% of his known income at the time. The trial court proceeed to sentence Thachankary to four years of rigorous imprisonment. While Thachankary had requested for a lighter sentence citing medical ailments, the Court opined that his position did not warrant leniency especially considering the magnitude of his abuse of power. The court also imposed a fine of ₹30.84 lakhs on Thachankary, the exact amount of disproportionate assets it found. Thachankary has now challenged this verdict before the Kerala High Court. The case originated from a complaint filed by Bobby Kuruvila, who claimed to be an anti-corruption crusader. He alleged that Thachankary had acquired houses, flats and other properties during his service disproportionate to his known income. A vigilance investigation launched subsequently found that Thachankary had acquired assets worth over ₹64 lakh between 2003 and 2007, which were disproportionate to his known income. Thachankary later moved the Vigilance Court seeking discharge, claiming that the assets were acquired through family shares and gifts. However, the Court rejected his plea. In 2021, the State government granted sanction for further investigation by a special unit of the Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB). However, Kuruvila moved the Kerala High Court, alleging that this was a move to delay the trial. In August 2025, a Division Bench of the High Court allowed the petition and set aside the government order allowing further investigation. The High Court also ordered a time-bound conclusion of the trial, on which the yesterday's verdict was pronounced.

items.title: Gurugram hit and run: Court remands accused Kalyan Bainsla to 14 days judicial custody
items.summary: A Gurugram court on Friday remanded Kalyan Bainsla, the driver accused of hitting a woman biker, and co-accused Lavneesh, to judicial custody for 14 days. Judicial Magistrate Ist Class (JMIC) Nidhi Beniwal passed the order after the police custody of the accused ended. They had earlier been remanded to the custody of Gururgam Police on Wednesday for two days following their arrest from Rajasthan on Tuesday. The accused have been arrested in a case registered by the Sector 55/56 Police Station under Sections 109 (attempt to murder), 281 (rash driving) and 125 (act endangering life or personal safety of others) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). The police have also invoked Section 78 (stalking) and 79 (word, gesture or act intended to insult the modesty of a woman) of the BNS against them. The case was registered after the victim, Shivani Chauhan, posted a video on social media on Sunday showing a vehicle allegedly driven by Bainsla, a gym owner, speeding towards her and hitting her bike on the Golf Course Road. The video was captured by a camera mounted on the bike. Chauhan, who goes by the name Sia on social media, is seen falling from her bike after the collision. She has accused Bainsla, referred to as Kalyan Singh in the court records, of harassing her before hitting her bike and of fleeing the spot after causing the accident. After the video went viral on social media, the police registered a suo motu case in the matter. However, the police initially did not invoke the offence of attempt to murder. It was later that Section 109 of the BNS was added to the case. The incident sparked national outrage with people demanding strict action against the car driver.

"Today we are told some youngsters are starting their own office without training. That is really not good. Unless you train with a senior you won’t know the real skills of advocacy, the real tricks of the trade, you will just be wondering. We know youngsters are ambitious. But unless you train with a senior, you won’t know the niceties of the profession. Nowadays, youngsters are so ambitious, but where are the soft skills? Every day from a senior you have to learn. We are concerned about the future of the Bar," it said. items.title: Reporter TV MD Anto Augustine moves Kerala High Court for bail in alcohol possession case
items.summary: Managing director of Malayalam news channel Reporter TV, Anto Augustine has moved a plea before the Kerala High Court seeking bail following his arrest on allegations of possessing liquor in excess of the legally permissible levels under the Kerala Abkari Act. items.title: DUSU Elections: Delhi HC bans victory processions; says candidates, student organisations have to pay damages for hooliganism
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Friday banned any victory processions after the declaration of the Delhi University Students' Union (DUSU) election results. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia said that no procession must be carried out by the candidates, their supporters, students or anyone else, either on the roads or inside the colleges and hostels. "It will be the responsibility of the Delhi Police to ensure that any such victory procession does not take place. Any violation shall not only attract criminal and administrative action against the students but shall also amount to contempt of court," the Bench ordered. Noting that there was violation of its previous orders and the Lyngdoh Committee recommendations during campaigning, the Court said that it will impose exemplary costs on all the major student organisations. It issued notice to all the 140 candidates contesting the DUSU elections and the prominent student organisations, directing them to explain why they should not be saddled with damages "Let notice to student organisations be issued. The list shall be provided by DU counsel. We request DU counsel to provide the list of 140 candidates who are contesting the elections of DUSU. Notices shall be issued to all these 140 candidates as well," the Court said. The Bench added that the Delhi Police must not shy away from taking action against these people merely because they are students. items.title: Navodaya schools: Why Tamil Nadu has opposed them for decades
items.summary: The Supreme Court, on Thursday, September 17, said Tamil Nadu has to change the “mindset” that Hindi cannot be taught on the soil of the state, cautioning that “individual States cannot act like individual countries”. The oral observations by Justice BV Nagarathna and Justice Augustine George Masih came during a hearing on the establishment of Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas (JNVs) in Tamil Nadu. The court also gave the state three more months to identify land in every district for setting up the schools, while asking the Union and Tamil Nadu state to resolve their differences through discussions. The dispute, however, goes beyond the question of Hindi. At its core are Tamil Nadu’s two-language policy, the role of the Union in education and whether a state can refuse to implement a centrally funded education scheme on the grounds that it conflicts with its own laws and policies. TVK government looking for a new Chief Secretary? | Powertrip #165 What are Navodaya schools? Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas are co-educational, residential schools run by the Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti under the Union Ministry of Education. The schools were established to provide education to students, particularly those from rural areas. Admission is primarily through an entrance examination for Class VI. The schools are funded by the Union government, while states are generally expected to provide land for their establishment. The scheme follows a three-language formula involving the regional language, Hindi and English. In Tamil Nadu, the language arrangement has been a key point of contention. Why has Tamil Nadu opposed Navodaya schools? Tamil Nadu has followed a two-language policy of Tamil and English for decades, in contrast to the three-language formula promoted by the Union government. The state’s language policy also has statutory backing through the Tamil Nadu Tamil Learning Act, 2006. The Act requires Tamil to be taught as a subject from Classes I to X. It provides for Tamil and English to be taught in schools, while students whose mother tongue is neither Tamil nor English can study their mother tongue as an optional subject. Tamil Nadu has argued that the three-language structure followed by Navodaya schools is incompatible with this framework. items.title: Keralam child rights panel asks schools to stop punishing students over long hair
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Schools in Keralam cannot punish, harass, or discriminate against students simply because they choose to wear their hair long, the Kerala State Commission for Protection of Child Rights has said. The Commission has recommended that students, irrespective of gender, should be free to grow and maintain their hair according to their personal preference, while schools should focus on their education and personality development rather than their physical appearance. The order, issued by Commission member P Shajesh Bhaskar on September 15, says that boys, girls, and children who have not affirmed their gender identity should have the freedom to grow their hair in a manner suited to their preference. It also says that students who have not affirmed their gender identity should have the right to choose their preferred dress code. The Commission specifically recommended that school authorities must not mentally harass students, remove them from class, discriminate against them, or subject them to other disciplinary action because of the length of their hair or related matters. At the same time, students who grow their hair have a responsibility to maintain it cleanly and safely, ensuring that it does not obstruct their eyes or face. During laboratory activities, sports competitions, and practical classes, students with long hair must tie it up or secure it with a hair band where necessary for safety. The Commission also said that applying chemicals or colours to hair in a manner that could harm students’ health is not advisable. The Commission said that the issue must be viewed in the context of gender equality in education. It noted that although schools in Kerala claim to be gender-neutral, discrimination against boys and children who do not identify with a particular gender continues. The Commission said students’ rights, individuality, abilities, and wellbeing, rather than gender-based distinctions, should be at the centre of education. items.title: Operation Toofan: Kerala police struggle to deal with addicts
items.summary: Kerala’s anti-narcotics campaign ‘Operation Toofan’, completed 100 days on September 9. The numbers are staggering: After the start of the campaign, till September 17, police have arrested 11,776 people in 10,918 cases. They also seized 23925.120 grams of MDMA and nearly 1457 kg of cannabis. But inside Kerala’s prisons and police stations, officers are confronting a different side of the drug problem: people exhibiting severe withdrawal symptoms, becoming violent in police stations and prisons, sometimes injuring themselves or others, and returning to drug use soon after they are released. One reason for this, according to investigators and mental health professionals, is the absence of protocols to identify what they have consumed or address their addiction when people are arrested with small quantities. Is Kerala’s war on drugs holistic? Aalam* was shaking and struggling to control himself while in police custody after being picked up during an Operation Toofan search. The 28-year-old migrant worker from Jharkhand said he was beaten both at the police station and inside prison, where fellow inmates accused him of being violent. “I get shivering and I might lose control. I had been using it for a while. I was beaten both in the police station and inside jail. Inside jail, I was beaten by other inmates. They said I was violent, but I don’t think I was,” Aalam, who was arrested twice under Operation Thoofan, told TNM. Aalam*, who lives in Perumbavoor in Ernakulam district, came to Kerala from Jharkhand six years ago and has worked in various odd jobs. He has wounds and bruises across his body.
